deep.reconstruction:
Top of page (numerical, purpose not fully determined). The page carries on the margin computation from the previous page. It has a column of number pairs (0.1, 5.2, 25.2, 82.23, …, 5. 29 20, 77 38, 101 51, 65 43, 13 4, 10 65 17, 37 11, 74) and scattered figures: 9721, 1+4·9721 = 38885, 46585, 44690, 10250, 17290, 3969 = 63², 23104 = 152², 13690, 32825, 12025, 925, 325.
- My own check: 9721 is prime, 9721 ≡ 1 (mod 8), and 9721 = 75² + 64². The work is probably number-theoretic, for example square roots or residues modulo the prime 9721, or a two-squares representation. The algorithm cannot be recovered with certainty.

Main derivation: two power series.
- φ(x) = 1 − x + x²/4 − x³/36 + … = Σ (−x)^k/(k!)². In modern terms φ = J0(2√x).
- ψ(x) = x − x²/2 + x³/12 − … = Σ (−1)^k x^{k+1}/(k!(k+1)!). In modern terms ψ = √x·J1(2√x).
- Gauss records the derivative rules φ' = −ψ/x (written 'ψ:x' after a correction) and ψ' = φ.
- Hence x²φ'' + xφ' + xφ = 0 (my inference). This is Bessel's equation of order 0 after the substitution x ↦ 2√x.

Repeated derivatives at a point n. Each derivative of φ is reduced to the form φ·P_k(1/n) + ψ·Q_k(1/n). The rule is d/dn(φP + ψQ) = φ(P' + Q) + ψ(Q' − P/n). Gauss obtains:
- φ' = −ψ/n
- φ'' = −φ/n + ψ/n²
- φ''' = ψ/n² + 2φ/n² − 2ψ/n³
- φ'''' = φ/n² − 4ψ/n³ − 6φ/n³ + 6ψ/n⁴

This serves the Taylor step φ(n+x) = φ(n) + xφ'(n) + …. Gauss writes it as 'φ(n+x) = φ − ψ/n', i.e. the first-order term with the factor x suppressed.

Coefficient table. The table on the lower left continues the same recursion. Rows alternate between P and Q coefficients of successive powers of 1/n:
- φ''': P = 2/n²; Q = 1/n² − 2/n³
- φ⁽⁴⁾: P = 1/n² − 6/n³; Q = −4/n³ + 6/n⁴
- φ⁽⁵⁾: P = −6/n³ + 24/n⁴; Q = −1/n³ + 18/n⁴ − 24/n⁵
- φ⁽⁶⁾: P = −1/n³ + 36/n⁴ − 120/n⁵; Q = 9/n⁴ − 96/n⁵ + 120/n⁶
- φ⁽⁷⁾: P = 12/n⁴ − 240/n⁵ + 720/n⁶; Q = 1/n⁴ − 72/n⁵ + 600/n⁶ − 720/n⁷
- φ⁽⁸⁾: P = 1/n⁴ − 120/n⁵ + 1800/n⁶ − 5040/n⁷; Q = −16/n⁵ + 600/n⁶ − 4320/n⁷ + 5040/n⁸

General ansatz. Gauss differentiates the general expression
F = φ(A/n^a + B/n^{a+1} + C/n^{a+2} + …) + ψ(A'/n^a + B'/n^{a+1} + …).
He obtains
F' = φ(A'/n^a + (B' − aA)/n^{a+1} + (C' − bB)/n^{a+2} + …) + ψ((−aA' − A)/n^{a+1} + (−bB' − B)/n^{a+2} + …),
with b = a+1. This is the device of undetermined coefficients for:
- writing derivatives of such expressions in the same φ,ψ form, and
- conversely finding antiderivatives (e.g. of φ·n^{−a}) as asymptotic series in 1/n.

Coefficient patterns (right side).
- Gauss tabulates S(a) = 6, 36, 120, 300, 630 for a = 3…7. These are exactly the second coefficients 6, 36, 120 of P for φ⁽⁴⁾, φ⁽⁶⁾, φ⁽⁸⁾, up to sign.
- He takes first through fourth differences: 30, 84, 180, 330; then 24, 54, 96, 150; then 30, 42, 54; then 12, 12.
- He states the closed form S(a) = a(a−1)(a−1)(a−2)/2.
- The first difference is S(a+1) − S(a) = (a−1)²a + (a−1)a² = (a−1)(2a−1)a.
- An auxiliary column gives 2, 9, 24, 50, 90 = a²(a−1)/2 next to the triangular numbers 1, 3, 6, 10, 15, for a = 2…6.
- Bracket symbols [n], ((n−1)/n)[n], [n−1], [n+1], 2n[2n] suggest a factorial-type notation for the general coefficient. This part is struck through and not reconstructible.

Purpose. The work appears aimed at numerical computation and asymptotic treatment of the Bessel-type function J0(2√x) (Taylor stepping, asymptotic integrals). The next page treats the related averages of (1 − g sin θ)^{−μ} by equally spaced sampling.
errors: 'φ(n+x) = φ − ψ/n' omits the factor x (and higher terms); as written it is the first-order Taylor term in shorthand, not an equality.
φ' = −ψ/x: the image shows a correction ('x − ψ:x' with strokes). The correct relation, consistent with the later φ' = −ψ/n, is φ' = −ψ/x.

All derivative formulas φ' through φ⁽⁴⁾, the full P/Q coefficient table up to φ⁽⁸⁾, the differentiation of the general ansatz, and the formula a(a−1)²(a−2)/2 with its difference a(a−1)(2a−1) check out correctly.
The numerical block at the top cannot be verified without knowing its purpose; no evident error.

results.what: φ = Σ(−x)^k/(k!)², ψ = Σ(−1)^k x^{k+1}/(k!(k+1)!), with φ' = −ψ/x and ψ' = φ
results.modern_name: Bessel functions J0(2√x) and √x J1(2√x); Bessel ODE in the variable x
results.usually_credited_to: D. Bernoulli / Euler (series, 18th c.), Fourier 1822, Bessel 1824

results.what: Reduction of the k-th derivative of φ to φ·P_k(1/n) + ψ·Q_k(1/n), with the coefficient table up to k = 8
results.modern_name: Recurrence for higher derivatives of Bessel functions / Taylor-series stepping for tabulation

results.what: Undetermined-coefficient ansatz φΣA_i n^{−a−i} + ψΣA'_i n^{−a−i} and its derivative
results.modern_name: Asymptotic expansion of integrals of Bessel functions by formal series (integration by parts in disguise)
results.usually_credited_to: 19th-century asymptotics (Poisson, Stokes, Hankel for Bessel asymptotics)

deep.surprise_reason: Gauss handling the series of J0(2√x) and J1 and their derivative recurrences is consistent with his known interest in such series and in numerical work. The material is correct but standard calculus. The asymptotic ansatz is only begun and is not carried to a new result.
